content:
If you're a heavy user of Apple Watch app betas this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

The related updates are being pushed through the App Store, with the update notes reading: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features have been added."

Apple notified developers this week that the entire process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems) is expected to be officially released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates are being pushed out well in advance.

Apple said this measure is needed due to issues with the arm64 segments of some watchOS apps. It is understood that Apple is automatically reprocessing and repackaging the apps to fix binary file compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue running without additional action from developers.
